title: Localized single-source cocycle evaluated on the cohomology sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $K$ a bounded-below derived abelian etale sheaf, $L$ a K-injective cochain complex, $r:K\cong QL$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, $W$ an etale neighbourhood, and $f:\mathbf Z[W]\to L^n$ a cycle. Use the free sheaf, localization and bounded-below Hom identifications of [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-injective-source-comparison], and the canonical germ comparison of [def-weil-pbc-canonical-derived-cohomology-germs]. The canonical germ comparison evaluated on the localized class of $f$, transported by the inverse bounded-below Hom identification, equals evaluation of $f$ lifted to cycles and then projected to $H^n(L)$, transported through the homology localization factorization and $H^n(r^{-1})$. This is equality of sections over $W$, without taking stalks or restricting to a strict henselization.

proof.text: the localization isomorphism sends the class of the single-source cocycle to its chain map into the shifted complex, then applies the quotient and shift comparison. Degree-zero homology of that map is the map on cycles followed by the homology quotient. The single-complex homology identification removes the source single complex. The homology shift comparison identifies the target with degree n homology of L. Naturality of the localization factorization and the homology shift comparison transports this equality along r inverse. Evaluation of the resulting sheaf morphism at the free generator is sourceFreeSectionsEquiv, giving the displayed section. This works for every integer n; zero cocycles give zero sections and boundaries give zero homology sections.
